questions.key_step: Rewrite in cos^2x (or cos2x) and take the range of a quadratic.

questions.key_step: Base change makes the equation a perfect square: log sin = 2 log cos.

questions.key_step: tan A = -tan B => sin theta + cos theta = n, n in {-1,0,1}; sum of n^2/2.
questions.justification: One non-obvious reduction plus careful enumeration of six angles in a numerical question with domain check.

questions.key_step: Product-to-sum cancels cos(3theta/2); union of two solution families; count positive/negative.
questions.justification: Numerical answer; identity step, union of families and counting needed.

questions.key_step: y = 9^(tan^2 x) gives y^2-10y+9=0; then tan^2(pi/12).
questions.justification: Substitution plus routine evaluation; options available.

questions.key_step: Split the polynomial so that sin^2 cos^2 (2 sin^2 - 1) factors; count roots in [0,2pi].
questions.justification: Factorisation is a little fiddly but standard; counting with endpoints is easy with options.

questions.key_step: Roots of cos = 1/3 in order => n = 13, then arithmetico-geometric sum.
questions.justification: Three stages (quadratic in sec, counting to fix n, AGP sum); counting n needs care.

questions.key_step: Divide by cos, square, reject the root with 4+5tan<0.
questions.justification: Standard a cos+b sin = c technique, one extraneous-root check.

questions.key_step: cos6x - sin6x = cos2x(1-sin^2cos^2) makes LHS constant 4; cubic x^3-x^2+2.
questions.justification: Several routine identities with one neat cancellation, then a cubic with an obvious root.

questions.key_step: 2sin^3+2 sin cos^2 = 2 sin x -> sin x = 2/3; count solutions to fix n=5.
questions.justification: Cancellation is easy to see; counting to n=5 is routine, then sign of roots.

questions.key_step: y = e^(sin x) gives 1+sqrt3 > e, so sin x > 1.
questions.justification: One familiar substitution and a comparison; short.

Factor (sin x-2)(a-2(sin x+2)); r via tan+cot=2/sin2x and exact values.

questions.key_step: Isolate 4cos-1 = 3 sin, square, choose the root using the interval.
questions.justification: Routine technique with options; rationalisation to match option.

questions.key_step: t = sin^2 2theta turns sin4+cos4, sin6+cos6 into linear forms; D>=0 then intersect with [0,1].
questions.justification: Identities, discriminant inequality and the range restriction; a slip changes the answer and no options.

questions.key_step: Spot the factorisation (sin x+3)(sin x-(x-1)^2) and count intersections.
questions.justification: Hidden factorisation plus a graphical count without options.
